newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina committee approves stadium tax vote.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina committee approves stadium tax vote.

text.p: North Carolina's Senate Finance Committee approved a proposal allowing voters in the 12-county Triad area to decide whether or not to raise sales taxes by one cent to finance a major league baseball stadium, a Senate clerk said Thursday.
The proposal (SB389) passed 19-4 in the committee and goes to the full Senate on Tuesday. It would then go to the House.
If approved, the tax would take effect only if the region wins one of the two Major League Baseball expansion teams scheduled to be awarded by 2000.

It would create a Triad Metropolitan Baseball Park Authority covering the 12 counties. Voters would then decide whether or not to enact a one-cent sales tax increase in all 12 counties for one year. The tax would raise about $145 million for a stadium to be built on the Forsyth-Guilford county line.

The stadium is expected to cost $210 million to $240 million, with the rest of the money put up by the team owners. The ownership group, led by Hickory resident Don Beaver, told lawmakers they would sign a 25-year lease for the stadium.
